Title: 4.9K views · 42 reactions | Anne Hampton "Annie" Potts is an actor known for many roles from her nearly 50-year career. She is known for her roles in the Ghostbusters and Toy Story franchises and her television roles, ranging from Designing Women in the mid-80s to Young Sheldon/Georgie & Mandy's First Marriage of today. She is 73 years old (October 28, 1952) and was born in Nashville.

Potts grew up in Franklin, Kentucky, in the rural south-central portion of the state along the Tennessee border. She earned a degree in theatre from Stephens College in Columbia, Missouri.
Potts began appearing in film and television in the late 70s. She appeared in several made-for-television movies and guest-starring roles in shows like Family, Remington Steele, and Magnum, P.I. She had a short regular role in Goodtime Girls.

In 1986, Potts was cast as Mary Jo Shively in the CBS sitcom Designing Women with Delta Burke, Jean Smart, Dixie Carter, and others. Potts appeared in all 163 episodes of the series over seven seasons. She also appeared in a reunion show in 2003.

In 1993, Potts was cast as Dana Palladino in Love & War. She appeared in about two-thirds of the show's episodes over three seasons. She earned an Emmy nomination for her work in 1994. She appeared in two short-lived series: Dangerous Minds and Over the Top in the mid-90s. She appeared in 88 episodes of the Lifetime original series Any Day Now from 1998 to 2002. She had recurring roles in shows such as Huff, Law & Order: Special Victims Unit, and Men in Trees. Since the turn of the millennium, she has guest-starred on shows such as Ugly Betty, Boston Legal, Two and a Half Men, Grey's Anatomy, and NCIS: New Orleans. She had a long-term recurring role in The Fosters from 2013 to 2018.

Starting in 2017, Potts appeared as Connie "Meemaw" Tucker, the grandmother of the title character in Young Sheldon. The show is a spin-off prequel to the long-running sitcom The Big Bang Theory. Young Sheldon followed its parent series as a big hit in the CBS lineup. The series concluded in 2024 after seven seasons. She has continued the role in Georgie & Mandy's First Marriage, a sequel to the prequel, which premiered in the fall of 2024. Last month, she started appearing as Aunt Sarah in the Fox series Best Medicine. Early reviews are positive. 

Primarily a television actor, Potts has appeared on the silver screen. Her first role was in Corvette Summer in 1978. She has appeared in five films in the Ghostbusters franchise, including the most recent Ghostbusters: Frozen Empire in 2024. She has voiced Bo Peep in the Toy Story franchise. Her voice is expected to be heard in the fifth installment when it is released around the summer solstice.  She has also voiced characters from both franchises in a series of video games. In 1986, she appeared with Molly Ringwald in Pretty in Pink and in Jumpin' Jack Flash as Liz Carlson. She appeared on Broadway in a revival of Pippin in 2014.

Potts founded The Heart Channels, a charity that aims to help people at the crossroads of their lives. She was seriously injured in a traffic accident in 1973. She has had several surgeries since, at least indirectly related to it, including a knee replacement in 2024 and a spinal fusion surgery last year. 

Potts (pictured left in 2025) married college sweetheart Steven Hartley in 1973, and they divorced in 1978. She married actor Greg Antonacci in 1978, and they divorced in 1980. He died in 2017. She has one son with filmmaker Scott Senechal. They married in 1981 and divorced in 1989. He died in 2025. She has two sons with television producer James Hayman (pictured right in 2024). They have been married for 35 years. They primarily live in the Toluca Lake neighborhood of Los Angeles. | Living Legend Bios

# Brian Bloom
## Life and career
After leaving the soap opera, Bloom starred in several made-for-television films with teen subjects, including _[Crash Course](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crash\_Course\_(film) "Crash Course (film)")_ (1988), _[Dance 'til Dawn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance\_'til\_Dawn "Dance 'til Dawn")_ (1988) and _[Desperate for Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desperate\_for\_Love "Desperate for Love")_ (1989). This enhanced his appeal for later roles, which included spots in _[Melrose Place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melrose\_Place "Melrose Place")_, _[2000 Malibu Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000\_Malibu\_Road "2000 Malibu Road")_, _[CSI: Miami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CSI:\_Miami "CSI: Miami")_, _[Law & Order: Special Victims Unit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law\_&\_Order:\_Special\_Victims\_Unit "Law & Order: Special Victims Unit")_, _[Drive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drive\_(2007\_TV\_series) "Drive (2007 TV series)")_ and [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO")'s _[Oz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oz\_(TV\_series) "Oz (TV series)")_. He played the role of fanatical cult leader Jonas Sparrow in the [Joss Whedon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Whedon "Joss Whedon") show _[Dollhouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dollhouse\_(TV\_series) "Dollhouse (TV series)")_. Bloom also starred in a series of 1994 television movies playing Bandit, a part loosely based on the [Burt Reynolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burt_Reynolds "Burt Reynolds") role.

# Brian Bloom
## Life and career
Bloom continued his working relationship with Joe Carnahan, playing private mercenary antagonist "Pike" in the 2010 movie _[The A-Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_A-Team\_(film) "The A-Team (film)")_, which Bloom also co-wrote with Carnahan, who directed the [20th Century Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/20th_Century_Fox "20th Century Fox") feature based on the [television series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_A-Team "The A-Team"). In 1989 Bloom starred alongside [Burt Lancaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burt_Lancaster "Burt Lancaster") in the 1990 miniseries _Voyage of Terror_, based on the 1985 [Achille Lauro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MS_Achille_Lauro "MS Achille Lauro") ship hijacking.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Bloom#cite_note-2)
Bloom also attended the sheriff’s academy and served as a reserve deputy with the Orange County Sheriff’s Department from 2001 to 2011. He is a certified self-defense expert and a Sifu of a rarefied street lethal modern Self Defense System called “Bojuka”. He has participated in combat seminars and taught use of force techniques to law enforcement, military and private security worldwide.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Bloom#cite_note-thedoorpost.com-3)
In 1997, Bloom developed and ran a .com hub known as AnimalWorldNetwork.com.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Bloom#cite_note-4) The website was an outpost for pet products, information, video content[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Bloom#cite_note-5) and celebrity pet lifestyle coverage, selling and shipping fair-trade, organic and holistic pet supplies with both brick and mortar locations and a robust online presence. Bloom sold the domain and business in 2007 for an undisclosed eight-figure deal.

# Brian Bloom
## Life and career
Bloom is well known for his long standing association with the _Call of Duty_ franchise, having performed voiceover and motion capture work in a majority of the franchise titles[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Bloom#cite_note-thedoorpost.com-3) culminating with the role of Captain Nick Reyes in _Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare_, a [first-person shooter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First-person_shooter "First-person shooter") video game by [Activision](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Activision "Activision"). Barrymore rose to prominence as a [child actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Child_actor "Child actor"). She established herself as a film star with leading roles in _[Poison Ivy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poison\_Ivy\_(1992\_film) "Poison Ivy (1992 film)")_ (1992), _[Boys on the Side](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boys\_on\_the\_Side "Boys on the Side")_ (1995), _[Scream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scream\_(1996\_film) "Scream (1996 film)")_ (1996), _[The Wedding Singer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wedding\_Singer "The Wedding Singer")_ (1998), _[Charlie's Angels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie's\_Angels\_(2000\_film) "Charlie's Angels (2000 film)")_ (2000), _[Charlie's Angels: Full Throttle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie's\_Angels:\_Full\_Throttle "Charlie's Angels: Full Throttle")_ (2003), and _[50 First Dates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/50\_First\_Dates "50 First Dates")_ (2004).

Her other film credits include _[Batman Forever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batman\_Forever "Batman Forever")_ (1995), _[Donnie Darko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donnie\_Darko "Donnie Darko")_ (2001), _[He's Just Not That Into You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/He's\_Just\_Not\_That\_into\_You\_(film) "He's Just Not That into You (film)")_ (2009), and _[Blended](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blended\_(2014\_film) "Blended (2014 film)")_ (2014).

He played the role of fanatical cult leader Jonas Sparrow in the [Joss Whedon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Whedon "Joss Whedon") show _[Dollhouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dollhouse\_(TV\_series) "Dollhouse (TV series)")_. # Brian Bloom
## Life and career
Bloom continued his working relationship with Joe Carnahan, playing private mercenary antagonist "Pike" in the 2010 movie _[The A-Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_A-Team\_(film) "The A-Team (film)")_, which Bloom also co-wrote with Carnahan, who directed the [20th Century Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/20th_Century_Fox "20th Century Fox") feature based on the [television series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_A-Team "The A-Team"). In 1989 Bloom starred alongside [Burt Lancaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burt_Lancaster "Burt Lancaster") in the 1990 miniseries _Voyage of Terror_, based on the 1985 [Achille Lauro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MS_Achille_Lauro "MS Achille Lauro") ship hijacking.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Bloom#cite_note-2)
Bloom also attended the sheriff’s academy and served as a reserve deputy with the Orange County Sheriff’s Department from 2001 to 2011. He is a certified self-defense expert and a Sifu of a rarefied street lethal modern Self Defense System called “Bojuka”. He has participated in combat seminars and taught use of force techniques to law enforcement, military and private security worldwide.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Bloom#cite_note-thedoorpost.com-3)
In 1997, Bloom developed and ran a .com hub known as AnimalWorldNetwork.com.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Bloom#cite_note-4) The website was an outpost for pet products, information, video content[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Bloom#cite_note-5) and celebrity pet lifestyle coverage, selling and shipping fair-trade, organic and holistic pet supplies with both brick and mortar locations and a robust online presence. Bloom sold the domain and business in 2007 for an undisclosed eight-figure deal.

Title: Rodd Redwing
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7
**Rodd Redwing / Rodric Redwing**
**Birth name: Webb Richardson / Ulysses Webb Richardson Jr.
1904 - 1971**
![Image 1](https://www.b-westerns.com/pic_m-r/nativeal.jpg)
**(Courtesy of Ed Phillips)**
**Above - Redwing in CATTLE
QUEEN OF MONTANA (RKO, 1954).**![Image 2](https://www.b-westerns.com/pic_m-r/nativeam.jpg)
**(Pressbook clipping courtesy of Les Adams)**  
**A familiar face in westerns and TV programs during the 1940s - 1960s was Chickasaw Indian Rodd Redwing.   
Redwing's real name was Webb Richardson, and he was born 1904 in Chattanooga, Tennessee to Lillian and Ulysses W. Richardson. His parents were African American and in census records, his father was an elevator operator and later, a barber. Mother Lillian was a hair dresser. They divorced in 1920.
In 1929, Webb Richardson was in New York City, acting in the play "Malinda" in Greenwich Village. A review mentions that it was an "all-colored dramatic-musical". (Link to an article on the play is further down this webpage.)
A few years later, he was In Hollywood pursuing an acting career ... and re-inventing himself as "Rodric Redwing". Confirmation of his arrival in Tinseltown were 1934 and 1936 Los Angeles voter registrations for Rodric Redwing, occupation "Actor".
His career spanned from the mid 1930s through his passing in 1971 and included many westerns, serials, and television shows. Most of his roles were portraying Native Americans.
He also was considered the fastest - or one of the fastest - quick draw artists and instructed many Hollywood personalities including Richard Widmark, Charlton Heston, Anthony Quinn, Glenn Ford, Alan Ladd, and Elvis Presley. He was also an expert showman with a whip, knives, and tomahawks.

I remember him in the cliffhanger, THE SON OF GERONIMO (Columbia, 1952). Clayton Moore starred - he was available during his year off from the Lone Ranger TV show (when John Hart portrayed the LR). Redwing has a lot of dialog and screen time portraying Geronimo's son 'Porico', and he's billed fourth behind Moore, Bud Osborne and Tommy Farrell. Moore and Redwing - and their doubles - have some great slugfests in later episodes in the serial.
Some Redwing movie and TV highlights:**
*   **he played the Gurkha Sergeant breaking trail for Errol Flynn and his paratroopers in OBJECTIVE BURMA (Warners, 1945).**  
*   **he was a cavalry trooper / Indian guide in LITTLE BIG HORN (Lippert, 1951) which starred Lloyd Bridges and John Ireland.**  
*   **he's Native American "Mr. Brother" in about a half dozen episodes of THE LIFE AND LEGEND OF WYATT EARP television program.**
**Some Redwing biographies mention that he did World War II military service. Found no supporting records on that. We do know that he worked in about ten films during 1942 - 1945. There was also a surprise - he's listed as a "waiter" in the 1942 Los Angeles City Directory.   
Movies and TV work, public appearances, and charity events kept him busy. Redwing also was a gunsmith for the Stembridge Gun Rental shop which was located on the Paramount studio lot. Among Rodd's jobs was as a "powder man" loading blank cartridges.
He was on a movie shoot in Spain for RED SUN (1971) which starred Charles Bronson. On his May 30, 1971 flight home to Los Angeles, he suffered a heart attack and died. He and wife Erika had no children.
The cremains of he and his mother Lillian are interred next to each other at Hollywood Forever (AKA Beth Olam Cemetery, Hollywood Memorial Cemetery), Hollywood, California.
He fibbed about his Native American lineage. But his Indian persona was dignified and sincere ... and he became a well respected member of the Hollywood movie community.**
**There's questions and confusion about his birth place, family name, and background. Below are three biography variations. There are more.

1. Redwing claimed he was a Chickasaw Indian. (See pressbook clipping at top of this webpage.) That lineage was summarized in an April, 1951 syndicated "Sights and Sounds from Hollywood" column by Gene Hanksaker. Excerpt:**
> **"He's a fascinating fellow, half Chicksaw [_sic_] and half Hindu. His India-born, Brahman father was a mind-reader on the Keith vaudeville circuit. His Mississippi born mother operated beauty parlors with her sisters in New York. There she met and married 'Prince Rajpurkaii'. Rod's original name was Rodric Ashmed Tokaji Hokar Kar Rajpurkaii."**
**2. A Rodd Redwing biography has been available for years at Wikipedia. Here's from April, 2022:**
> **"Rodd Redwing (August 24, 1904 - May 29, 1971) was an American actor and a noted quick-draw artist with a six-gun. He claimed to be Native American, although in the 1940 United States Census, his birthplace was listed as India and some sources reported his real name was Roderick Rajpurkaii Jr. He was also known as Roderic Redwing and Rodric Redwing."**
**3. In 2023, there was a significant revision to his Wikipedia biography. Redwing was Black, not Native American. And the updated bio provides more on his early life before he became "Rodd Redwing":**

> **"Rodd Redwing (August 24, 1904 - May 29, 1971) was born Webb Richardson on August 24, 1904 in Tennessee, USA. His father, Ulysses William Richardson (b. 1873), was Black and was an elevator man from Tennessee. His mother, Lillian Webb (b. 1878), was also Black and worked as a manicurist and hairdresser. Lillian divorced her husband William in 1920. Their son Webb moved to New York to pursue a career in acting and appeared in the 1929 musical 'Malinda' in Greenwich Village with a cast of African American performers. Webb later changed his birthname to Redwing, adopted a Native American identity, and changed his birthplace to New York City. Some sources reported that he used the Hindu-sounding name Roderick Rajpurkaii Jr. and said his father was a Brahmin mind reader from India."**
![Image 3](https://www.b-westerns.com/pic_m-r/print22.jpg)**Angela Aleiss, PhD, is author of _Hollywood's Native Americans: Stories of Identity and Resistance_ (Praeger, 2022) and has taught at CSU Long Beach and UCLA.  
Her research included Native American "pretenders" such as Webb Richardson who became Rodd Redwing. Angela's book may have been the impetus for that recent Wikipedia update.
She and I exchanged e-mails over the past few years on Redwing. Special thanks to Angela for help and hints on his real life.**
**On the trail of Rodd Redwing**
**Richardson family info is available in the census for 1910, 1920, and 1930 and a few other records. And the Richardson family home address is consistent - 517 Georgia Avenue, Chattanooga, Tennessee.   
His full birth name MAY be Ulysses Webb Richardson Jr. and I've highlighted his name variations in
this color:**

*   **1910 census summary and census takers worksheet - 5 year old Webb Richardson (born Tennessee; race Mulatto) was living with his parents at 517 Georgia Avenue, Chattanooga, Hamilton County, Tennessee. His 38 year old father was Julius [_sic_] W. Richardson (born U. S.; race Mulatto; occupation "Elevator Man") and mother was 32 year old Lillian (born Tennessee; race Mulatto; occupation "Hairdresser"): [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:MG6B-1DM](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:MG6B-1DM)**  
*   **World War I draft registration dated September 12, 1918 for 45 year old Ulysses William Richardson. He and wife Lillian Webb Richardson lived at 517 Georgia Avenue, Chattanooga, Tennessee; he was Black; born March 1, 1873; and was an "Elevator Man" at the Chattanooga Post Office and Custom House: [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:KZ6W-GG9](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:KZ6W-GG9)**  
*   **May 1, 1920 _Chattanooga, Tennessee News_ reported that Lillian Webb 'Lillie' Richardson filed for divorce from Ulysses William Richardson. She was a hair dresser and masseur. He was an elevator man and now a well known barber: [https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-chattanooga-news-lillian-webb-lilli/122997908/](https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-chattanooga-news-lillian-webb-lilli/122997908/)**  

*   **1920 census summary and census takers worksheet - owning their home at 517 Georgia Avenue, Chattanooga, Tennessee were 46 year old Ulysses W. Richardson (born Tennessee; race was Black; occupation "Barber"). With him was 15 year old son Ulysses W. Richardson Jr. (born Tennessee; race was Black): [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:MNPZ-L4X](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:MNPZ-L4X)**  
*   **1930 census summary and census takers worksheet - son Webb was no longer with his father in Chattanooga. And the census taker had spelling problems with names Ulysses and Richardson. 56 year old Ulysis W. Richerdson (born Tennessee; race was Black; occupation "Barber Shop") and 37 year old wife Susie M. Richerdson (born Tennessee; race was Black) own their home at 517 Georgia Avenue, Chattanooga, Tennessee: [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:SP43-LY3](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:SP43-LY3)**  
*   **Webb was in New York City and the December 11, 1929 _Brooklyn, New York Daily Eagle_ has an article on the play "Malinda", and actor Webb Richardson was in the cast of this "an all-colored dramatic-musical": [https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-brooklyn-daily-eagle-webb-richardson/133245327/](https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-brooklyn-daily-eagle-webb-richardson/133245327/)**  

*   **1930 census summary and census takers worksheet - 26 year old Webb Richardson (born Tennessee about 1904; occupation "Actor - Motion Pictures") is one of four roomers living with 48 year old widow Birdie Johnson and her children at 2014 Fifth Avenue, New York City. He was Black; father was born in Tennessee and mother in Mississippi: [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X4L4-8QS](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X4L4-8QS)**
**Records with the "Redwing" name begin in the mid 1930s:**

*   **Ancestry.com had the 1934, 1936 and 1938 Voter Registrations for Los Angeles County - Rodric Redwing (occupation "Actor") lived at 1422 North Kingsley Drive.**  
*   **Social Security application dated February 27, 1937 for 32 year old Rodric Redwing - he was born August 24, 1904 in New York City; parents were Ulysses William Richardson and Lillian Redwing; he was Indian; was living in Los Angeles; and employer was Central Casting, Hollywood.**  
*   **1940 census summary and census takers worksheet - 35 year old Rodric? Redwing (born India; occupation "Actor - Pictures") and his 28 year old wife Erika (born Germany) were lodgers living at 1749 La Brea, Los Angeles, California: [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:K9C6-2S4](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:K9C6-2S4)**  
*   **Fold3 Military records had his World War II draft registration dated February 14, 1942 - 37 year old Rodric Redwing was born August 24, 1904 in New York City. He and wife Erika lived at 1439 1/2 North Tamarind Avenue, Los Angeles, California. Employer was "Central Casting Corp". He was 5 feet, 10 1/2 inches tall, weighed 162 pounds, and race was "Indian".**  
*   **1942 Los Angeles City Directory has Roderic Redwing as a "waiter" and living at 1437 Tamirand Ave: [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:815L-5YZM](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:815L-5YZM)**

_**Sisters**_ is an American [family drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television) "Drama (film and television)") television series that aired from May 11, 1991, to May 4, 1996, on [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC"). The series was created by [Ron Cowen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Cowen "Ron Cowen") and [Daniel Lipman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Lipman "Daniel Lipman"), who were also the executive producers and showrunners.

_Sisters_ focused on four very different sisters living in [Winnetka, Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winnetka,_Illinois "Winnetka, Illinois"). Their recently deceased father, Thomas Reed, a [doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_doctor "Medical doctor"), had been absent and a [workaholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workaholic "Workaholic"), while their long-suffering mother, Beatrice, turned to alcoholism to cope with his neglect and affairs. Having always wanted sons, their father had called the girls by male versions of their full names: Alexandra was called Alex; Theodora, Teddy; Georgiana, Georgie; and Francesca, Frankie.
For the first two seasons, each episode began with the sisters' weekly ritual of chatting in a [steam bath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauna "Sauna") together,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sisters_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sisters_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-oconnor-3) but switched to a more traditional opening sequence beginning with the 1992–1993 season: glossy, black-and-white filmed scenes of the sisters engaging in various activities during both their childhood and adult years. Initially, the only soundtrack used for the opening was the sounds of the characters, but in the fall of 1993 a piano solo composed by [John Debney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Debney "John Debney") was added as theme music.
Most episodes of the show featured a number of [flashbacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flashback_(narrative) "Flashback (narrative)"), in which the characters would interact with or simply observe their younger selves (played by younger actresses).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sisters_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-oconnor-3) Although the show was a drama with soap opera–style storylines,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sisters_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-oconnor-3) the show was also quirky and offbeat in the style of other shows at the time like CBS's _[Northern Exposure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern\_Exposure "Northern Exposure")_.

Now divorced from John, Georgie goes to graduate school in psychology. She begins a relationship with Brian ([Joe Flanigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Flanigan "Joe Flanigan")), a 24-year-old student in her classes who was very standoffish to her at first. Teddy and Cat are carjacked; Cat meets police officer Billy Griffin ([Eric Close](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Close "Eric Close")) when reporting the crime. Later, Teddy is accidentally shot in the head with the gun she bought for protection. She falls into a coma, but Alex convinces brilliant neurosurgeon Dr. Gabriel Sorenson ([Stephen Collins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Collins "Stephen Collins")) to operate and save her life. Teddy eventually begins a relationship with Sorenson, and Cat decides to enter the police academy. Charley (now played by [Sheila Kelley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheila_Kelley_(American_actress) "Sheila Kelley (American actress)")) becomes a foster parent to Jesse ([Sean Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Nelson_(actor) "Sean Nelson (actor)")), the son of a woman at her free clinic who died. She also begins dating her colleague Dr. Wes Hayes ([Michael Whaley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Whaley "Michael Whaley")), though he is initially resistant to an interracial relationship. Reed (now played by Noelle Parker) returns to town after divorcing Kirby and losing custody of her daughter Halsey, and ends up running a high-priced call-girl ring. Alex turns crucial evidence over to the police and Reed is sentenced to community service. Teddy and Gabe decide to marry, but their wedding is interrupted when a heart donor is found for Big Al; Teddy and Gabe finally marry at the hospital just before Big Al is taken into surgery. Charley decides to adopt Jesse, and plans to quickly marry Wes because two parents make a more appealing adoptive family; however, Charley eventually realizes Jesse should instead be adopted by the family that had already adopted his brother. Charley and Wes marry anyway. Alex's talk show is canceled again and she decides to take an extended trip to help flooding victims in Tennessee. In the final episode, Georgie's college thesis about her sisters deeply angers Alex and Charley, though Teddy finds it amusing. The sisters must put aside their differences when Beatrice has a major stroke.

Shortly before Beatrice dies Frankie returns from Japan and clashes with Charley. Later, Frankie announces she wants to move back home to Winnetka. Georgie sees John at Bea's memorial service and realizes she misses him; shortly afterward, she breaks up with Brian. The sisters scatter their mother's ashes on the rosebushes she named after them. Teddy announces she is pregnant with a daughter, who she plans to name Beatrice Rose. Georgie and John discuss reconciling and share an embrace. Finally, Alex assumes the role of family matriarch.
[![Image 2](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/2/20/Sisters_maincast.jpg/250px-Sisters_maincast.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sisters_maincast.jpg)

_**Sisters**_ is an American [family drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television) "Drama (film and television)") television series that aired from May 11, 1991, to May 4, 1996, on [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC"). The series was created by [Ron Cowen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Cowen "Ron Cowen") and [Daniel Lipman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Lipman "Daniel Lipman"), who were also the executive producers and showrunners.
texts.2:
_Sisters_ focused on four very different sisters living in [Winnetka, Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winnetka,_Illinois "Winnetka, Illinois"). Their recently deceased father, Thomas Reed, a [doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_doctor "Medical doctor"), had been absent and a [workaholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workaholic "Workaholic"), while their long-suffering mother, Beatrice, turned to alcoholism to cope with his neglect and affairs. Having always wanted sons, their father had called the girls by male versions of their full names: Alexandra was called Alex; Theodora, Teddy; Georgiana, Georgie; and Francesca, Frankie.
For the first two seasons, each episode began with the sisters' weekly ritual of chatting in a [steam bath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauna "Sauna") together,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sisters_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sisters_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-oconnor-3) but switched to a more traditional opening sequence beginning with the 1992–1993 season: glossy, black-and-white filmed scenes of the sisters engaging in various activities during both their childhood and adult years. Initially, the only soundtrack used for the opening was the sounds of the characters, but in the fall of 1993 a piano solo composed by [John Debney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Debney "John Debney") was added as theme music.
Most episodes of the show featured a number of [flashbacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flashback_(narrative) "Flashback (narrative)"), in which the characters would interact with or simply observe their younger selves (played by younger actresses).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sisters_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-oconnor-3) Although the show was a drama with soap opera–style storylines,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sisters_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-oconnor-3) the show was also quirky and offbeat in the style of other shows at the time like CBS's _[Northern Exposure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern\_Exposure "Northern Exposure")_.
texts.8: Now divorced from John, Georgie goes to graduate school in psychology. She begins a relationship with Brian ([Joe Flanigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Flanigan "Joe Flanigan")), a 24-year-old student in her classes who was very standoffish to her at first. Teddy and Cat are carjacked; Cat meets police officer Billy Griffin ([Eric Close](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Close "Eric Close")) when reporting the crime. Later, Teddy is accidentally shot in the head with the gun she bought for protection. She falls into a coma, but Alex convinces brilliant neurosurgeon Dr. Gabriel Sorenson ([Stephen Collins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Collins "Stephen Collins")) to operate and save her life. Teddy eventually begins a relationship with Sorenson, and Cat decides to enter the police academy. Charley (now played by [Sheila Kelley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheila_Kelley_(American_actress) "Sheila Kelley (American actress)")) becomes a foster parent to Jesse ([Sean Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Nelson_(actor) "Sean Nelson (actor)")), the son of a woman at her free clinic who died. She also begins dating her colleague Dr. Wes Hayes ([Michael Whaley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Whaley "Michael Whaley")), though he is initially resistant to an interracial relationship. Reed (now played by Noelle Parker) returns to town after divorcing Kirby and losing custody of her daughter Halsey, and ends up running a high-priced call-girl ring. Alex turns crucial evidence over to the police and Reed is sentenced to community service. Teddy and Gabe decide to marry, but their wedding is interrupted when a heart donor is found for Big Al; Teddy and Gabe finally marry at the hospital just before Big Al is taken into surgery. Charley decides to adopt Jesse, and plans to quickly marry Wes because two parents make a more appealing adoptive family; however, Charley eventually realizes Jesse should instead be adopted by the family that had already adopted his brother. Charley and Wes marry anyway. Alex's talk show is canceled again and she decides to take an extended trip to help flooding victims in Tennessee. In the final episode, Georgie's college thesis about her sisters deeply angers Alex and Charley, though Teddy finds it amusing. The sisters must put aside their differences when Beatrice has a major stroke.
texts.9:
Shortly before Beatrice dies Frankie returns from Japan and clashes with Charley. Later, Frankie announces she wants to move back home to Winnetka. Georgie sees John at Bea's memorial service and realizes she misses him; shortly afterward, she breaks up with Brian. The sisters scatter their mother's ashes on the rosebushes she named after them. Teddy announces she is pregnant with a daughter, who she plans to name Beatrice Rose. Georgie and John discuss reconciling and share an embrace. Finally, Alex assumes the role of family matriarch.

**Rodd Redwing / Rodric Redwing**
**Birth name: Webb Richardson / Ulysses Webb Richardson Jr.
1904 - 1971**
![Image 1](https://www.b-westerns.com/pic_m-r/nativeal.jpg)
**(Courtesy of Ed Phillips)**
**Above - Redwing in CATTLE
QUEEN OF MONTANA (RKO, 1954).**![Image 2](https://www.b-westerns.com/pic_m-r/nativeam.jpg)
**(Pressbook clipping courtesy of Les Adams)**  
**A familiar face in westerns and TV programs during the 1940s - 1960s was Chickasaw Indian Rodd Redwing.   
Redwing's real name was Webb Richardson, and he was born 1904 in Chattanooga, Tennessee to Lillian and Ulysses W. Richardson. His parents were African American and in census records, his father was an elevator operator and later, a barber. Mother Lillian was a hair dresser. They divorced in 1920.
In 1929, Webb Richardson was in New York City, acting in the play "Malinda" in Greenwich Village. A review mentions that it was an "all-colored dramatic-musical". (Link to an article on the play is further down this webpage.)
A few years later, he was In Hollywood pursuing an acting career ... and re-inventing himself as "Rodric Redwing". Confirmation of his arrival in Tinseltown were 1934 and 1936 Los Angeles voter registrations for Rodric Redwing, occupation "Actor".
His career spanned from the mid 1930s through his passing in 1971 and included many westerns, serials, and television shows. Most of his roles were portraying Native Americans.
He also was considered the fastest - or one of the fastest - quick draw artists and instructed many Hollywood personalities including Richard Widmark, Charlton Heston, Anthony Quinn, Glenn Ford, Alan Ladd, and Elvis Presley. He was also an expert showman with a whip, knives, and tomahawks.
texts.1:
I remember him in the cliffhanger, THE SON OF GERONIMO (Columbia, 1952). Clayton Moore starred - he was available during his year off from the Lone Ranger TV show (when John Hart portrayed the LR). Redwing has a lot of dialog and screen time portraying Geronimo's son 'Porico', and he's billed fourth behind Moore, Bud Osborne and Tommy Farrell. Moore and Redwing - and their doubles - have some great slugfests in later episodes in the serial.
Some Redwing movie and TV highlights:**
*   **he played the Gurkha Sergeant breaking trail for Errol Flynn and his paratroopers in OBJECTIVE BURMA (Warners, 1945).**  
*   **he was a cavalry trooper / Indian guide in LITTLE BIG HORN (Lippert, 1951) which starred Lloyd Bridges and John Ireland.**  
*   **he's Native American "Mr. Brother" in about a half dozen episodes of THE LIFE AND LEGEND OF WYATT EARP television program.**
**Some Redwing biographies mention that he did World War II military service. Found no supporting records on that. We do know that he worked in about ten films during 1942 - 1945. There was also a surprise - he's listed as a "waiter" in the 1942 Los Angeles City Directory.   
Movies and TV work, public appearances, and charity events kept him busy. Redwing also was a gunsmith for the Stembridge Gun Rental shop which was located on the Paramount studio lot. Among Rodd's jobs was as a "powder man" loading blank cartridges.
He was on a movie shoot in Spain for RED SUN (1971) which starred Charles Bronson. On his May 30, 1971 flight home to Los Angeles, he suffered a heart attack and died. He and wife Erika had no children.
The cremains of he and his mother Lillian are interred next to each other at Hollywood Forever (AKA Beth Olam Cemetery, Hollywood Memorial Cemetery), Hollywood, California.
He fibbed about his Native American lineage. But his Indian persona was dignified and sincere ... and he became a well respected member of the Hollywood movie community.**
**There's questions and confusion about his birth place, family name, and background. Below are three biography variations. There are more.
texts.2:
1. Redwing claimed he was a Chickasaw Indian. (See pressbook clipping at top of this webpage.) That lineage was summarized in an April, 1951 syndicated "Sights and Sounds from Hollywood" column by Gene Hanksaker. Excerpt:**
> **"He's a fascinating fellow, half Chicksaw [_sic_] and half Hindu. His India-born, Brahman father was a mind-reader on the Keith vaudeville circuit. His Mississippi born mother operated beauty parlors with her sisters in New York. There she met and married 'Prince Rajpurkaii'. Rod's original name was Rodric Ashmed Tokaji Hokar Kar Rajpurkaii."**
**2. A Rodd Redwing biography has been available for years at Wikipedia. Here's from April, 2022:**
> **"Rodd Redwing (August 24, 1904 - May 29, 1971) was an American actor and a noted quick-draw artist with a six-gun. He claimed to be Native American, although in the 1940 United States Census, his birthplace was listed as India and some sources reported his real name was Roderick Rajpurkaii Jr. He was also known as Roderic Redwing and Rodric Redwing."**
**3. In 2023, there was a significant revision to his Wikipedia biography. Redwing was Black, not Native American. And the updated bio provides more on his early life before he became "Rodd Redwing":**
texts.3:
> **"Rodd Redwing (August 24, 1904 - May 29, 1971) was born Webb Richardson on August 24, 1904 in Tennessee, USA. His father, Ulysses William Richardson (b. 1873), was Black and was an elevator man from Tennessee. His mother, Lillian Webb (b. 1878), was also Black and worked as a manicurist and hairdresser. Lillian divorced her husband William in 1920. Their son Webb moved to New York to pursue a career in acting and appeared in the 1929 musical 'Malinda' in Greenwich Village with a cast of African American performers. Webb later changed his birthname to Redwing, adopted a Native American identity, and changed his birthplace to New York City. Some sources reported that he used the Hindu-sounding name Roderick Rajpurkaii Jr. and said his father was a Brahmin mind reader from India."**
![Image 3](https://www.b-westerns.com/pic_m-r/print22.jpg)**Angela Aleiss, PhD, is author of _Hollywood's Native Americans: Stories of Identity and Resistance_ (Praeger, 2022) and has taught at CSU Long Beach and UCLA.  
Her research included Native American "pretenders" such as Webb Richardson who became Rodd Redwing. Angela's book may have been the impetus for that recent Wikipedia update.
She and I exchanged e-mails over the past few years on Redwing. Special thanks to Angela for help and hints on his real life.**

this color:**

Title: Dominic Kalipersad on Instagram: "Did you know that three leading actors in the 1990s US TV series The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air were of Trinidadian descent?

Alfonso Ribeiro, Tatyana Ali, and Karyn Parsons portrayed all three of the Banks children.

Alfonso Ribeiro: 
Born Sept. 21, 1971, in NYC in the U.S.  to Trinidadian parents Joy Ribeiro and Michael Ribeiro, (and the paternal grandson of Trinidadian calypsonian Albert Ribeiro, known as Lord Hummingbird), he began his career at age 8, but is probably best known for his most prominent role as Carlton Banks, the cousin of Will Smith’s lead character on “Fresh Prince” from Sept. 1990 to May 1996.

Tatyana Ali:
Born on Jan. 24, 1979, in the US to a Sheriff Ali, a retired police officer from Trinidad, and Sonia Ali, a nurse from Panama, she is a Harvard graduate. She began her career in entertainment at the age of four, appearing on the children’s television show Sesame Street. In 1990, Ali landed the role of Ashley Banks on “Fresh Prince”, which launched her into stardom.

Karyn Parsons:
Born Oct. 8, 1966, to a Trinidadian mother, Louise (Hankerson) Parsons, and a French-Canadian father, Kenneth B. Parsons, she had her first TV role in the NBC drama The Bronx Zoo (1987), but she made her big break as Will Smith’s cousin, Hilary Banks, on The Fresh Prince of Bell Air.

There were other actors in guest starring roles, including Nia Long whose maternal grandparents were from Trinidad.

In “Fresh Prince”, Long portrayed the role of  Lisa Wilkes who almost married Will Smith.
